name: Gradient 3D and glass
region: the United States, worldwide on the web
summary: A mark lit like an object: top highlights, gradients from light to deep colour, a glass bevel, a reflection under it and a soft drop shadow. The screen was now the main medium, and the mark imitated a polished button or a globe.

philosophy.core_thesis: On a screen a mark can be a lit object: gloss, depth and reflection make it feel new, touchable and alive.
design_principles: Light the mark from the top: a gradient from 20–30% lighter at the top to the base colour at 60% of the height.
Add a gloss highlight: a white shape at 40–70% opacity over the top 40–50% of the mark.
Model the volume with a bevel or a sphere: shading from the base colour to 30–40% darker at the edge.
Add a floor reflection: a mirrored copy at 20–30% opacity, faded over 30–40% of the mark height.
Use 2–4 hues of high saturation; a gradient counts as its two end colours.
Keep the silhouette simple, a globe, a bubble, a rounded square, so the lighting reads at 32 px.
anti_patterns: A flat fill with no light
Fine line detail under 3% of the mark height
A mark that has no one-colour version in the manual

construction.grid: A rounded square or a circle as the base shape; the highlight is an ellipse at 80–90% of the width, set in the top half.
construction.geometry: Spheres, bubbles, rounded rectangles with corner radii of 20–25% of the height, and swooshes.
construction.stroke_rule: No stroke as a line; forms are fills with a 1–2 px light rim at the top edge.
construction.symmetry: Mirror symmetry on the vertical axis for the base shape; light from the top or the top left.
construction.detail_floor: No detail under 3% of the mark height; the gloss shape is at least 25% of the height.

form.silhouette: A sphere, a bubble, an orb or a rounded square at 1:1, often over a reflection that adds 30% to the height.
form.ornament: Gloss highlights, a reflection, a soft shadow and sparkles; no line ornament.
form.letterforms: Rounded sans in bold, lower case, often with the same gloss or a drop shadow; set apart from the orb.

colour.strategy: Saturated blues, greens and oranges in vertical gradients, with white gloss and a soft grey shadow.
colour.reversal_rule: The manual must add a flat one-colour silhouette; the gloss, the reflection and the shadow drop out.

reproduction.clear_space: A quarter of the orb height on each side, plus the reflection under it.
reproduction.media: Screens first: web headers, desktop and phone icons; print in CMYK with care for the gradients.

evidence.title: Wikipedia puzzle globe, version 2
evidence.credit: Version 1 by Nohat (concept by Paullusmagnus); Wikimedia Foundation

emotion.target_response: Shiny novelty: the viewer sees a polished, touchable object and feels the promise of new technology.

use_cases: app icons with a retro theme
avoid_when: The mark must print in one colour on paper or fabric.
The brief asks for a serious, durable or institutional tone.

modifiers.how: Keep the silhouette and the hues; drop the gloss, the reflection and the shadow, and fill each part with one flat colour.
Keep the orb; put it inside a closed ring with the name on the ring, and reduce the gloss to one highlight.
